arguments.analyst: Historical evidence: conservative polar/isosteric edits near the chromophore-adjacent sites are tolerated (O6 N164S:S175G 3.538; O8 H81L:Y106F 3.528), while chromophore-proximal aromatic substitutions H77Y (O7 3.759) and M88V (O9 3.722) retain high brightness. Double edits generally score near the 3.5-3.7 band; bulk/charge-disrupting multisite combos (O4, O5 ~1.3) collapse. Menu singles like N144Y, E115A, K209N sit at ~3.695, suggesting residue-identity changes at those positions are not strongly penalized.
arguments.hypothesis: Pairing one conservative surface edit (K156R, N105S, N23S) with a tolerated aromatic/polar core-adjacent substitution (H77R, N144Y, Y106C-class) will preserve brightness at or above the 3.56-3.70 band, since O7/O9 show chromophore-near conservative swaps remain bright and O6/O8 show double edits stay near 3.5-3.6.

decision.critic: Estimates span only 3.567-3.607 with wide uncertainty (0.08-0.20); C47 highest but least certain, so ranking rests on fitted predictions, not measurement.
